findings.claim: When graph.json resolves and exists but manifest.json is missing or unloadable, doctor misattributes the Manifest::load failure to source detection, reporting "source detection failed: {error}" even though detect() succeeded or never ran — a health-check tool whose purpose is accurate diagnosis emits a wrong cause.
findings.evidence: In doctor(): `let freshness = detect(root, &DetectOptions {...}).map(|detection| Manifest::load(&manifest_path, Some(root)).is_unchanged(&detection.files, ManifestKind::Ast));` followed by `Err(error) => fail_check("graph_freshness", format!("source detection failed: {error}"))`. The Manifest::load error is funneled into the same Err arm as a detect() failure.
findings.suggested_fix: Match on detect() and Manifest::load() separately so a missing/corrupt manifest produces a distinct "could not load graph manifest" detail (or a dedicated manifest_presence check), keeping load failure distinct from detection failure.

findings.claim: Bundle/MCP-config file reads reject symlinks via entry.file_type()/symlink_metadata and then open the path in a separate syscall, so a writer with access to the bundle directory can swap a verified regular file for a symlink between the check and File::open, defeating the documented symlink-rejection guarantee for content that is then hashed and credential-scanned.
findings.evidence: collect_files_bounded_with_limits: `if file_type.is_symlink() { return Err(...) }` then later `let bytes = read_file_with_limit(&path, limit)` which does `fs::File::open(path)` with no O_NOFOLLOW; SECURITY.md excerpt added in this diff states validate "rejects symlinks" while treating bundles as untrusted.
findings.suggested_fix: Open with O_NOFOLLOW (std::os::unix::fs::OpenOptionsExt::custom_flags / equivalent guarded Windows handling) or verify symlink_metadata on the opened file handle, so the symlink check and the read are the same object.

findings.claim: `--project=`/`--user=` (and `--project-root=`/`--user-root=`) with an explicitly empty value are silently accepted as an empty root path, while the space-separated forms error on a missing value, yielding an inconsistent boundary and a doctor run against "" instead of a usage error.
findings.evidence: parse_doctor_options: `root = PathBuf::from(value.split_once('=').map_or("", |(_, value)| value));` — for `--project-root=` this produces PathBuf::from("") with no error, unlike `required_value` which returns "error: --project-root requires a value".
findings.suggested_fix: Route the `=` forms through the same non-empty validation: `let v = value.split_once('=').map_or("", |(_, v)| v); if v.is_empty() { return Err(...) }`.

findings.claim: `compass agent validate --platform <NAME>` silently ignores the platform requirement for managed-install bundles, even though the help text says the option "Require[s] a matching exported platform" without qualification.
findings.evidence: validate_path: `if root.join("manifest.json").is_file() { validate_export_bundle(root, expected_platform) } else if root.join(".compass-install.json").is_file() { validate_managed_bundle(root) }` — expected_platform is dropped on the managed path; help.rs page for "agent validate" documents `--platform <NAME>  Require a matching exported platform`.
findings.suggested_fix: Either reject --platform when the target is a managed install, or document that the option applies only to exported bundles.

findings.claim: normalize_manifest_roots re-serializes both manifests through serde_json::to_vec_pretty before comparison, so byte-level differences in formatting or key ordering between direct and generic installs are normalized away and can no longer be detected by the byte-identical tree assertion.
findings.evidence: `let mut manifest: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_slice(bytes)?; manifest["root"] = ...; *bytes = serde_json::to_vec_pretty(&manifest)?;` applied to both trees before `assert_eq!(generic_tree, direct_tree)`.
findings.suggested_fix: Compare the parsed serde_json::Value of the manifests (with root normalized) for semantic equality, and separately compare raw bytes after a targeted byte-level replacement of the known root string, so formatting drift still fails the test.
